title: Patterns in the booking system
idea: Incorporating design patterns means adding a pattern only where the booking system has a real change point, such as overlap rules or who hears about a booking.
points: Start from a change you expect, then pick the pattern that isolates it.
Strategy pattern: `ConflictPolicy` lets `BookingService` swap overlap rules without edits.
Observer pattern: `NotificationService` and `AuditLogger` subscribe to new bookings.
Each pattern should remove an `if` chain or a hard-wired call, not add ceremony.

code.title: Strategy: ConflictPolicy
code.caption: Times are hours as numbers, so `0.25` is 15 minutes. Add a policy whose `conflicts` always returns `false` and run it again.

walk.text: `ConflictPolicy` is the interface: it takes a candidate slot and the room's existing bookings.
`StrictOverlapPolicy` rejects only slots that truly overlap; back-to-back is fine.
`BufferPolicy` also blocks slots that come within the gap of a booking, before or after it.
`BookingRepository` stores bookings, so the service holds no list of its own.
The repository and policy are injected, so the service never names a concrete rule.
The overlap decision is delegated to whichever policy was passed in.
One loop runs the identical bookings under both policies.

code.title: Observer: booking listeners
code.caption: The service tells every subscriber about a booking. It never imports the notifier or the logger.

walk.text: `AuditLogger` is the c05-t05 class: `record(event, fields)` writes JSON to an injected sink.
`NotificationService` is an observer with one `onBooked` method and one job.
The service keeps a private list and lets anyone subscribe.
`book(employeeId, roomId, start, end)` keeps the c05-t01 contract, then tells every listener in order.
A small listener adapts `onBooked` to `audit.record`, so `AuditLogger` stays unchanged.
Wiring happens outside the service, so adding a listener needs no edit there.

pitfalls: Do not add a pattern because it is famous; name the change it absorbs.
Keep observers free of booking rules, or the order they run starts to matter.
Avoid a Factory for one concrete class; a constructor call is clearer.

quiz.why: With a half-hour gap, `10.25 < 10.5` clashes. A start of `10.5` is not below `10.5`, so it is allowed.

takeaway: Each pattern in your design should absorb one change you can name.
